subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Four-Stroke Cycle
description: A quick win: understand The Four-Stroke Cycle.

hook.text: Every gasoline engine repeats four steps—intake, compression, power, exhaust—thousands of times a minute.

buildup.text: First the piston drops, sucking in fuel and air. Then it rises to squeeze the mixture tight.

discovery.text: A spark ignites the compressed mix, slamming the piston down—that single stroke moves the car.

twist.text: Only one of the four strokes produces power. The other three just prepare and clean up.

climax.text: Nikolaus Otto patented this cycle in 1876, and nearly every gasoline engine still uses it today.

punchline.text: One stroke does the work, three strokes set it up.

quiz.question: How many of the four strokes actually produce power?
